body.statement: There is a universal numerical choice of \(C_{\mathrm{sel}}>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), \[\max\left\{\sup_{P\in\mathcal G_n:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}Q_P(\phi_n=1),\ \sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n(\delta_n):(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}Q_P(\phi_n=0)\right\}\le p_{\mathrm{sel},n}=\min\left\{1,C_{\mathrm{sel}}\left[(s_n/\delta_n)^2+\{\rho_n(\alpha/16)/\delta_n\}^2\right]\right\}.\]
body.justification: The explicit two-sided pretest error controls the fallback contribution to non-Gaussian expected length.
body.gap: Fixed-cumulant ACE bounds do not quantify branch-selection errors for nuisance-contaminated residual cumulants at shrinking separation.
body.consumer: It lets an interval implementation report a finite-sample upper bound on selecting the wrong score branch.
